decisions.reason: The product builds on the already accepted BASIC 518 and shows a positive early market signal, so performance appears above aspiration and this established firm has little reason to withdraw it quickly.
A dedicated product-page launch suggests real commitment, and in this broad mobile processing portfolio the firm likely keeps the shredder while sales and customer feedback accumulate.

Its lower website prominence points to more uncertainty, but the mobile high-speed grinder fits the firm's core markets and an experienced machinery maker usually gives such a product more than one year to prove itself.
The stationary electric fine shredder matches the firm's strategic move toward tougher and more resource-saving processing solutions, so even with uncertain early results it is likely retained.

This green-waste-focused grinder is somewhat more exposed because it is a narrower variant and may overlap with other grinders, but it still fits the customer base and is likely kept during the trial period.
A standalone presentation and strong fit with the firm's stationary recycling equipment business indicate enough strategic importance and slack to keep the pre-shredders on the market.
